The '''1887 Puerto Rico census''' was the ninth population census held in [[Puerto Rico]] and the last census count under [[Government of Spain|Spanish rule]]. Under Spanish rule, censuses had been taken at irregular intervals in Puerto Rico between 1765 and 1887.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www2.census.gov/prod2/decennial/documents/1980/proceduralHistory/Chapter_11.pdf |title=Chapter 11: Puerto Rico and the Outlying Areas |publisher=[[United States Census Bureau]] |accessdate=2024-12-24}}</ref>
The population count was 798,565 - an increase of 66,917 or 9.0% over the previous census in 1877.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://rcm1.rcm.upr.edu/demografia/wp-content/uploads/sites/30/2020/04/Vazquez-1968-Crecimiento-poblacional-de-Puerto-Rico-1493-al-presente.pdf |title= EL CRECIMIENTO POBLACIONAL DE PUERTO RICO 1493 AL PRESENTE|accessdate=8 February 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://censo.estadisticas.pr/censo-decenal/Puerto-Rico/1887|title= 1887 (Instituto Nacional de Estadísticas de España)|website=censo.estadisticas.pr|accessdate= 8 February 2025}}</ref> 
After 1887, the following Puerto Rican census of 1899 was held during US rule.

==Race==
{{Seealso|Afro–Puerto Ricans|White Puerto Ricans}}
The 1887 census had two primary race options; one for white people and one for "colored" people (non-white). At 474,933 people, 59.5% of the population was [[White Puerto Ricans|white]]. The total "colored" population was 323,632 people. 246,647 people were sub-classified as [[Mulatto|Mulattos]], making up 76.2% of the total non-white population.<ref name="archive.org">{{cite web|url=https://archive.org/stream/reportoncensusof00unitiala#page/58/mode/2up |title=Report on the census of Porto Rico, 1899 Census of "Porto Rico"|page= 57|date=1900|accessdate= December 24, 2024}}</ref>
